items.title: ANSWER:
items.description:
ANSWER:

A. Gaia

Before Gaia, we had tracked 118,000 stars. Gaia has since mapped over 1.8 billion. By using a billion-pixel camera 1.5 million kilometers from Earth, this mission increased our precise star data by 10,000 times, effectively “restarting” the map of our galaxy.

items.title: ANSWER
items.description:
ANSWER

False:

The Big Dipper isn't actually a constellation at all; it's an asterism. It is a smaller part of the constellation Ursa Major. We don't know which constellation was the first to be named, but Taurus was one of the earliest to be named.
